body: If this repo tooling supports it, we can start using [`assert`](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/release-notes/typescript-3-7.html#assertion-functions) functions so that the TS compiler understands that for this code path, those variables exist.
Any particular reasons for this change?

isFiniteNumber already does that, but since we saved it to variables, it doesn't work in all cases. I didn't want to risk making too many changes here (since the variables were chosen to make the final equation not too complex). Not sure what you prefer
undefined isn't a valid value according to the type, since `x?: y` isn't the same as `x: y | undefined`
I prefer boundaries, but the property in the renderState which is called `start`, so I went with the same

body: Fine—we can introduce this pattern in future PRs. The main advantage is that we don't need to use `!` at every use, but only assert that the variable exists in the scope (it'll also be handy in our `index` widget where the lifecycle mutates the "class variables").
Right, we might as well change the type in the Helper then?

the type in the helper is `numericRefinements: { [facet: string]: SearchParameters.OperatorList }`, do you think that should be `numericRefinements: { [facet: string]: SearchParameters.OperatorList | undefined }`? I feel like we'd need to change a couple more types for that to be consistent. I'd rather keep the delete, it's not a performance footgun anymore nowadays

with https://github.com/algolia/algoliasearch-helper-js/pull/801 we can use this for dispose instead (much cleaner IMO)

```js
        return state
          .removeDisjunctiveFacet(attribute)
          .removeNumericRefinement(attribute);
```
